schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
schemes.summary: Crop insurance scheme giving financial support to farmers who suffer crop loss or damage from natural calamities, pests and diseases, at a low farmer-paid premium.

schemes.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
schemes.summary: Central sector financing facility (Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare) that gives medium- and long-term loans through banks and other lenders for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets, with a 3% per year interest subvention and credit guarantee support.

beneficiary.description: Farmers, FPOs, PACS and other cooperative societies, SHGs, JLGs, agri-entrepreneurs, start-ups and government-sponsored PPP projects (list taken from lender summaries of the official guidelines)

criteria: The project must be a viable post-harvest management project (for example warehouses, cold storage, grading and sorting units, pack houses, ripening chambers) or a community farming asset, including infrastructure for smart and precision agriculture.
The applicant must own the project land or hold a valid lease of it.
The applicant must meet the lending institution's credit norms.
Interest subvention and credit guarantee apply to loans up to Rs. 2 crore per project.

Fresh loan disbursement under the scheme was scheduled to complete by the end of FY 2025-26, while the scheme itself runs to 2032-33 for subvention and guarantee support. Whether new loans are still being sanctioned in FY 2026-27 could not be confirmed - check with the lending bank.

benefits.summary: Loans from banks and financial institutions with 3% per year interest subvention on loans up to Rs. 2 crore for a maximum of 7 years (including a moratorium of up to 2 years). Credit guarantee cover through CGTMSE for loans up to Rs. 2 crore, with the guarantee fee borne by the Government; for FPOs the guarantee can come from the facility under the FPO promotion scheme. PIB states the interest rate on these loans is capped at 9%. A collateral-free term loan of up to Rs. 2 crore is available.

schemes.name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
schemes.summary: Online trading platform of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare that links e-NAM-enabled mandis (APMCs) so that farmers, traders and FPOs can register and trade through transparent bidding with payments directly into bank accounts.

beneficiary.description: Farmers (sellers), traders and FPOs/FPCs trading at e-NAM-enabled mandis

criteria: Farmers can register on e-NAM as sellers and choose the APMC/mandi where they want to trade; the selected APMC approves the registration after KYC.

Trading takes place at mandis that are integrated with e-NAM. A state integrates its mandis by adopting a single unified trading licence, a single-point market fee and e-auction/e-trading as a mode of price discovery.
Only commodities notified for e-NAM trading at the mandi can be traded there, so crop coverage depends on the mandi.

FPOs/FPCs can register on the e-NAM portal or mobile app, or at the nearest e-NAM mandi, by giving the FPO name, the name, address, email and contact number of the authorised person (MD/CEO/Manager) and bank details.

benefits.summary: Registration is free. Farmers get better price discovery through transparent bidding, access to more markets and buyers, real-time information on prices and arrivals in nearby mandis, and quick payments by RTGS, NEFT or BHIM UPI directly into their bank accounts. Assaying lets the price reflect the produce quality, and each arrival is digitally recorded with a unique lot ID that can be tracked from a mobile phone.

items.note: No fee for registration on e-NAM.
Instant payment into the seller's bank account via RTGS, NEFT or BHIM UPI.

On the portal, choose Registration Type 'Farmer', select the desired APMC and give a correct email ID, where the temporary login ID and password are sent.
Log in to the dashboard, open 'Click here to register with APMC', and fill in or update your details; the application goes to the selected APMC for approval after KYC.
Track the status (Submitted / In progress / Approved / Rejected) by email or on the dashboard.
After the APMC approves, you receive a permanent Farmer Login ID and password by email; you can also contact the mandi/APMC directly.

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme (Soil Health & Fertility component of RKVY)
schemes.summary: Scheme that helps state governments issue Soil Health Cards to farmers: a report on the nutrient status of each land holding with recommendations on fertilisers, bio-fertilisers and soil treatments. Launched on 19 February 2015; since 2022-23 it is a component of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) called 'Soil Health & Fertility'.

beneficiary.description: All farmers (a card is issued for each land holding)

criteria: The scheme is applicable to all farmers in India (cited by PIB from NITI Aayog).
A Soil Health Card is issued for each land holding.

benefits.summary: Soil testing of the holding on 12 parameters (N, P, K, S; Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B; pH, EC, organic carbon) and a printed/digital Soil Health Card with recommendations on the right amount of fertilisers, bio-fertilisers, organic inputs and soil treatments. The Central Government provides Rs. 190 per sample to the states to cover collection, testing, card generation and distribution. Cards are available in 22 languages.

items.note: Paid to states for collection, testing, card generation and distribution.

documents.notes: A secondary source says the card can be looked up on the portal with an Aadhaar number; not stated in the PIB document.

steps: Soil samples are collected from the field by trained personnel, agriculture department staff or agriculture-college students, using GPS-tagged grid sampling (2.5 hectares in irrigated areas, 10 hectares in rain-fed areas), after harvest or when no crop is standing (PIB).
Samples are tested in approved soil testing laboratories; results go to the national Soil Health Card portal, which generates the card with fertiliser recommendations (PIB).
To ask for sampling or to get your card, contact your local agriculture office, KVK or soil testing lab (secondary sources; not stated in the PIB document).

schemes.name: PM-KUSUM (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyaan)
schemes.summary: MNRE scheme to de-dieselise and solarise agriculture: Component A (small grid-connected solar plants of 500 kW-2 MW), Component B (standalone solar agriculture pumps up to 7.5 HP) and Component C (solarisation of grid-connected pumps, individually or by feeder).

beneficiary.description: Individual farmers (Components B and C-IPS); farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs and Water User Associations (Component A)

criteria: Component B: individual farmers can install standalone solar agriculture pumps of up to 7.5 HP in off-grid areas where grid supply is not available (replacing diesel pumps). Pumps above 7.5 HP are allowed but central support is limited to the 7.5 HP level.

Component C (Individual Pump Solarisation): farmers with an existing grid-connected agriculture pump of up to 7.5 HP; solar PV capacity up to two times the pump capacity in kW is allowed; surplus power can be sold to the DISCOM.

Component A: renewable power plants of 500 kW-2 MW can be set up by individual farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs or Water User Associations (or through a developer or the local DISCOM if they cannot arrange the equity).
Component C (Feeder Level Solarisation) is carried out by states/DISCOMs and is not an individual-farmer application.
Applicability in a given year depends on the state: MNRE gives each state an allocation and the state implementing agency invites and processes applications.

The MNRE page lists the scheme period as 'Till 31.03.2026'. Later MNRE memoranda reported in the press extended project timelines for already-sanctioned projects and PM-KUSUM 2.0 is still being finalised - confirm with your state implementing agency whether applications are open.

In the North Eastern states, Sikkim, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands: central assistance of 50%, state subsidy of at least 30%, and at most 20% paid by the farmer. Farmers may install pumps with central assistance even where a state does not provide its share.

beneficiary.description: Farmers (higher rate for SC/ST, small and marginal farmers and North Eastern states), women farmers (30% of funds earmarked), FPOs, SHGs, cooperatives and rural entrepreneurs

criteria: Individual farmers can receive a subsidy on eligible farm machinery through Direct Benefit Transfer; the rate is higher for SC/ST farmers, small and marginal farmers and beneficiaries in North Eastern states.
Women farmers are part of the target group and 30% of total funds are earmarked for them.
FPOs, SHGs, cooperatives and rural entrepreneurs can set up Custom Hiring Centres and Farm Machinery Banks.
The scheme runs through state Annual Action Plans: the Centre-State funding pattern is 60:40 for most states, 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan states and 100% Central for Union Territories.

beneficiary.description: Individuals, groups of farmers/growers, firms, SHGs, FPOs, companies, cooperatives, local bodies, APMCs and State Governments (as listed for the cold-storage component)

criteria: Assistance for cold storage (construction, expansion, modernisation of capacity up to 5,000 MT) is available to individuals, groups of farmers/growers/consumers, partnership and proprietary firms, SHGs, FPOs, companies, corporations, cooperatives, cooperative marketing federations, local bodies, APMCs and marketing boards, and State Governments.

Cold storages above 5,000 MT and up to 10,000 MT are covered by a separate National Horticulture Board scheme, not by MIDH.
MIDH covers many other horticulture activities; only the cold-storage component could be confirmed from the official sources read.

Minimum membership at the time of the Cabinet approval was 300 farmers in plain areas and 100 in North Eastern and hilly areas (secondary reports of the Cabinet decision).
Formation of the 10,000 FPOs has been reported as completed (secondary source); whether new FPOs can still be formed under this scheme could not be confirmed - ask SFAC, NABARD or NCDC.

benefits.summary: Per FPO: financial assistance of up to Rs. 18 lakh for 3 years; matching equity grant of up to Rs. 2,000 per farmer member with a limit of Rs. 15 lakh per FPO; and a credit guarantee facility up to Rs. 2 crore of project loan from an eligible lending institution.
